content_of_post_to_comment: Has anyone else realised that they have weird little sayings passed down from their slightly dotty but very lovable grandparent? And when you yourself use them, you get looked at like you’ve got three heads? My favourite is: just enough blue sky to make the sailor a pair of trousers.
comment: Those phrases are tiny family time capsules. The funny part is how language carries a history that disappears when the original storyteller is gone. I wonder how many expressions survive only because someone keeps saying them.
